design_rationale: The study is described as an open-label randomized controlled trial where neonates were randomly assigned 1:1 using a computer-generated randomization schedule.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed using sequentially numbered opaque sealed envelopes opened by an independent clinician, and baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Neonates with clinical seizures were randomly assigned to receive either PB or LEV with a 1:1 allocation as per a computer-generated randomization schedule and using sequentially numbered, opaque and sealed envelopes. When an eligible neonate was eligible to be enrolled, the envelope was opened by a clinician who was not part of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although open-label, the intervention was administered according to a strict predefined clinical protocol in an intensive care unit, deviations from protocol are not evident, and all randomized neonates were analyzed according to their assigned group.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Design: Open labelled, Randomized controlled trial. ... If seizures persisted even after correction of hypoglycemia and hypocalcemia, neonates were randomized for intervention to receive either LEV (20 mg/kg) or PB (20 mg/kg) intravenously.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data for the primary outcome (seizure cessation at 24 hours) were complete for all 100 randomized neonates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Allocated to LEV 50 ... Analyzed 50; Allocated to PB 50 ... Analyzed 50

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessment was clinical and subjective without EEG verification or blinding of the assessors in an open-label trial, introducing potential risk of bias in outcome measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Design: Open labelled, Randomized controlled trial. ... Termination of seizure was defined clinically if there were no abnormal movement/ eyeball deviation/nystagmus, no change in heart rate, no change in respiration/saturation and autonomic dysfunction. ... The limitation of our study was that we did not perform electroencephalographic monitoring to docu- ment cessation of seizure activity.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was registered retrospectively in April 2018 (CTRI/2018/04/013161) after the study had completed recruitment (conducted November 2014 to April 2016), precluding verification of a prospective analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial Registration: Clinical Trial Registry of India (CTRI/2018/04/013161). ... The proportion of patients achieving cessation of seizures following the first or second dose of the drug (PB or LEV), and those remaining seizure-free for next 24 hours was considered as the primary outcome.

overall_summary: The overall judgment is some concerns due to potential bias in outcome assessment arising from the unblinded clinical evaluation of seizure cessation without EEG monitoring, as well as retrospective trial registration.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated using computer-generated random numbers in blocks of four, with sealed opaque envelopes for allocation concealment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed using sequentially numbered sealed opaque envelopes handled by an independent person, and baseline characteristics were comparable.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Block randomization of 80 numbers in blocks of four was done using computer generated random numbers. They were put in serially numbered opaque envelopes and sealed. This was done by a person not involved in study.

domain_judgments.rationale: This was an open-label study where personnel were aware of assigned treatments, with potential crossover upon initial failure according to a clinical protocol, though analyzed by intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Our trial was an open-label trial, so the doctors and nursing staff were aware of the treatment assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Substantial attrition occurred before the 1-year follow-up (18 deaths during NICU stay and 14 of 62 survivors lost to follow-up, representing 40% missing data overall) with no sensitivity analysis or imputation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Among 62 discharged babies, 14 were lost to follow-up, and 48 babies (25 babies in LEV group and 23 babies in PB group) were followed at 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of clinical seizure cessation and adverse events were assessed without blinding by treating clinicians, introducing high risk of detection bias for subjective clinical evaluations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Lack of blinding of clinical outcomes, inability to monitor serum drug level and cerebral function, small sample size, and unavailability of bedside EEG were the limitation of our study.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan to confirm that reported outcomes were not selectively chosen.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Statistical analysis was done using intention to treat analysis. Results were analyzed using SPSS 23 software.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high due to substantial loss to follow-up for 12-month outcomes and unblinded assessment of subjective clinical outcomes including seizure control and adverse effects in an open-label trial.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that it is a randomized prospective trial where newborns were randomly assigned to receive phenobarbital or levetiracetam.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although random assignment is stated, no information is provided regarding the method of sequence generation or allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Newborns were randomly assigned to receive PB and LEV in a blinded manner.

domain_judgments.rationale: Interventions followed standard dosing guidelines in a NICU setting with all 30 randomized infants receiving treatment as assigned without notable protocol deviations or dropouts affecting the intended intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This was a randomized, one-blind prospective study conducted on term newborns receiving PB or LEV as ﬁrst-line treatment for seizure control.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data for the Hammersmith Neonatal Neurological Examination at baseline and 1-month follow-up were available and analyzed for all 30 randomized infants.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The Hammersmith score was evaluated by trained neonatologists of our NICU...

domain_judgments.rationale: No published trial registration or pre-specified statistical analysis plan was provided to rule out selective reporting of subscale outcomes and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We performed the Hammersmith Neonatal Neurological Examination (HNNE) at baseline (T0) and after one month of treatment (T1).

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to lack of details regarding the randomization and allocation concealment procedures, unclear blinding of outcome assessors for the clinical neurological evaluation, and absence of a pre-registered protocol.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial in which neonates were randomly assigned to either the levetiracetam or phenobarbitone group using a simple random lottery method.

domain_judgments.rationale: While a lottery method was used for random sequence generation, no details regarding allocation concealment are provided, though baseline characteristics appear reasonably balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After necessary exclusion and inclusion criteria randomization was done by simple random method; i.e.by lottery method with replacement.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was open-label, but neonates could not be aware of assignment and treatments followed standard clinical protocols with all 50 allocated per group analyzed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Intravenous loading dose (20mg/kg) of inj. Phenobarbital to control group and loading dose (50mg/kg) of inj. Levetiracetam to intervention group were given... Decision regarding further for treatment in case of treatment failure was made on the basis of institutional treatment protocol.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data for the primary and secondary endpoints are reported for all 100 enrolled neonates (50 in each group) with no apparent missing data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Table-I shows basic demographic data of the neonates with seizure. Out of 50 neonates each of intervention group and control group, respectively...

domain_judgments.rationale: Seizure control was determined purely by subjective clinical examination without blinding or continuous EEG confirmation, making outcome assessment highly susceptible to assessor bias in an open-label trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were monitored round the clock and clinically examined and seizure frequency, antiepileptic medication and adverse events were documented. Study end point was up to 48 hours but if seizure was not controlled within 48 hours it was labeled as treatment failure. Seizures were diagnosed clinically. No continuous EEG monitoring was performed at time of diagnosis and enrolment.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan to confirm that reported outcomes and analyses were not selected post-hoc.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The outcome variables were seizure control, times taken to be seizure free, and hospital stay.

overall_summary: The study is at overall high risk of bias primarily due to unblinded subjective clinical assessment of neonatal seizures without electroencephalographic (EEG) confirmation, compounded by unclear allocation concealment and lack of a pre-registered protocol.

design_rationale: The authors explicitly describe the study as an open-label randomized controlled trial where participants were randomized using computer-generated numbers and sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence generation was random and allocation concealment was properly maintained with sequentially numbered opaque sealed envelopes opened by an independent worker, with balanced baseline characteristics.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was done using computer generated numbers. Labelled slips were put in serially numbered opaque and sealed envelopes. They were opened when an eligible baby was enrolled by an independent worker, not worked in the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although open-label, the interventions were administered according to a strict standardized protocol, neonates cannot be biased by knowledge of intervention, and an intention-to-treat approach was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The team members managing the babies were aware of the treatment allocation... Statistical analysis It was done using intention to treat analysis on SPSS 10.

domain_judgments.rationale: Data on the primary outcome of clinical seizure control were complete and available for all 60 randomized participants (30 in each group).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thirty babies were randomized to levetiracetam group and 30 to phenobarbitone group ( Figure 2)... domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was clinical assessment of subtle/motor seizures, which is subjective and assessed by bedside treating team members who were explicitly unblinded to treatment allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Clinical control of seizure activity was the primary outcome variable of this study. Seizures were considered to be controlled if the baby was seizures free 24 hrs after last seizures... The team members managing the babies were aware of the treatment allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or pre-published protocol is referenced or provided to rule out selective reporting of outcomes or analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Clinical control of seizure activity was the primary outcome variable of this study. Seizures were considered to be controlled if the baby was seizures free 24 hrs after last seizures. Secondary outcomes were safety profile of levetiracetam, electrical seizures after control of clinical seizure, time taken to control seizures, and neurological examination till 6 months.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to the unblinded clinical assessment of seizure control by treating physicians and the absence of a pre-registered trial protocol or statistical analysis plan.
